judgements.justification: B's YH9r (1 h, confidence 2) gave 7 and named the forward algorithm 'a new algorithm' as the key contribution, but line 13 credits it to Vovk and to Azoury and Warmuth.
FknY raised 4 to 5 after the appendix step was answered, npqJ's main point (forward bound adds little) was never answered, and jxuz kept a 6, which is above threshold.
A rejected on limited significance and the d-factor gap, not by refusing credit for rebuttal promises; both committees heard the same parity concession and promised experiments.
No reviewer in either committee stated a changed position that differs from an unedited score.
Neither area chair called in an additional reviewer.
The gap is about significance and correctness of the central claims, not clarity verdicts tied to reviewer expertise.
WQsZ raised to 7 with a stated reason; 4n5Q's 2021-08-29 edit has no evidence of a silent raise against its own text.
Neither area chair discounted a low rating for lack of engagement; A's ratings all counted and B had no low rating.
B's acceptance rested on four consensus ratings with no recorded advocate; 4n5Q's 8 had no post-rebuttal text and itself said the algorithms are 'not that different most of the time'.
No reviewer admitted partial reading with high confidence; YH9r did not check the proofs but rated at confidence 2.
No committee contested the premise from a different theoretical tradition; A's objections were within the paper's own regret framework.
B's four-sentence meta-review cites only reviewer consensus that the paper 'should be accepted' and gives no reason for a spotlight.

A's FknY and npqJ checked the bounds against the classical VAW bound and cited the textbook exercise, small-loss work and Abbasi-Yadkori et al., while B's reviewers took the 'better bounds' as stated and scrutinised proofs and figures.
A's meta-review matches its reviewers' positions; B's 'inputs' misstatement concerns the paper, not reviewers, and is not toward a lower decision.
No reviewer or chair in either committee raised a narrow-audience or venue-fit objection.
B had no low-scoring detractor, and A's low scores rest on correct readings.
The authors posted no new experiments to either forum; they gave concessions and promises to both.
B gave a spotlight in line with 4n5Q's 8, and A's highest-confidence reviewer FknY rated low, not above the others.
No reviewer added a new objection and changed the score after the response period; FknY's unanswered 2021-08-31 request did not change its score.

B's verbal assessments were more favourable than A's, listing the better bounds and the lower bound as strengths, so the rating gap tracks a different judgement; stage 1 marks no same-facts weighting difference.
A's npqJ called the title 'somewhat misleading' and 'unbounded rewards' overstated, and A held the paper below acceptance on overstated bounds, while B took the claims at face value.
Neither committee had flat marginal-accept scores; A rated 5, 6, 5, 5 and B rated 7, 7, 7, 8.
